entries.source: Problem 1B (4.0 points) The circuit, shown in the figure on the left, consists of a capacitor with the capacitance [[0]] = 100 μF, an ideal diode, a constant voltage source [[1]] = 10.0 V, three identical resistors with the resistance [[2]] = 10.0 kΩ and a switch. At the initial moment, the capacitor is not charged and the switch is open. When the switch is shorted, the current through the diode goes for the time interval τ = 462 ms, and then stops. 1. Find the current through the diode immediately after shorting the switch. 2. Find the total charge that has flowed through the diode. Problem 1C (3.0 points) At the vertices of the regular 17-gon, there are 17 identical lenses. The optical centers of the lenses are located exactly at the vertices of the polygon, the planes of all lenses are perpendicular to one of the sides adjacent to the lens. The focal lengths of the lenses are all equal to [[3]] and coinciude with the length of the side of the 17-gon. entries.source: Problem 2 (10.0 points) Physics in the mountains The atmosphere of a real planet, such as the Earth, has a rather complex structure in view of the great variety of processes and phenomena involved in its formation. In this problem we will consider two simple models of the lower layer of the atmosphere, called the troposphere, which extends to an altitude of 10-15 km above the Earth's surface. To understand the physics of some phenomena it is sufficient to consider the Earth's atmosphere consisting of a single- component diatomic gas with the molar mass [[0]] .
entries.ko:
문제 2 (10.0점)
산에서의 물리
지구와 같은 실제 행성의 대기는 형성 과정에 관여하는 다양한 과정과 현상 때문에 상당히 복잡한 구조를 가진다. 이 문제에서는 지표면 위 10–15 km 높이까지 뻗어 있는 대기의 하층인 대류권에 대해 두 가지 단순한 모형을 다룬다. 일부 현상을 이해할 때에는 지구 대기가 몰 질량 [[0]]인 단일 성분 이원자 기체로 이루어졌다고 보아도 충분하다.

entries.source: Part 1. Isothermal atmosphere In the atmosphere, the lowest near-surface layer has an almost constant temperature, as it is heated up by the surface of the Earth. Therefore, we assume in this part that the temperature of the atmosphere remains the same over its entire altitude and is equal to [[0]] К, and the air pressure at the Earth's surface is [[1]] . Assume that the acceleration of gravity [[2]] is independent of the altitude above the Earth's surface, since the total height of the atmosphere is much less than the Earth's radius [[3]] . The universal gas constant is [[4]] .
